note: Statements the website may make from the 3-D simulation, and statements it must not make. Every number is an ESTIMATE (推估) and must carry its range. Basis: METHOD.md and results-simulation.json (signed 2026-11-27).

may.zh: 推估：等一個紅燈，人行道上機車排出的一氧化碳，換算成15分鐘平均約增加0.1–4 ppm，遠低於世界衛生組織的87 ppm。
may.en: Estimate: waiting through one red light adds about 0.1–4 ppm of carbon monoxide to your 15-minute average, far below the WHO value of 87 ppm.
may.basis: S1, S1-from, A, S5-12b: one red's contribution to a 15-min mean at kerb 0.5 m (P50 0.07–1.1 ppm, P95 up to 4 ppm; near-calm near-field NF1-fine P50 5 ppm)
may.mustCarry: 推估 / Estimate; range 0.1–4 ppm (up to about 5 directly behind a tailpipe in near-calm air); open street; one red; 15-minute averaging

may.zh: 推估：就算整整15分鐘每個紅燈都站在路邊、風一直從機車吹向你，一氧化碳平均約3–16 ppm，仍低於87 ppm。
may.en: Estimate: even standing at the kerb through every red for 15 minutes with the wind blowing from the scooters to you, carbon monoxide averages about 3–16 ppm, still below 87 ppm.
may.basis: S1-from and S5-12b stay-through with a fresh pack every red, child and pushchair height
may.mustCarry: 推估 / Estimate; range 3–16 ppm; extrapolated from one simulated red; rare held wind

may.zh: 推估：例外是嬰兒車停在一台怠速機車排氣管正後方約半公尺、幾乎無風且風向不變，連續15分鐘每個紅燈都在：這時一氧化碳15分鐘平均可能超過87 ppm（約十分之一到五分之一的情形）。
may.en: Estimate: the exception is a pushchair parked about half a metre directly downwind of an idling scooter's tailpipe, in near-still air that keeps its direction, through every red for 15 minutes: then the 15-minute carbon monoxide average can pass 87 ppm (in about 1 in 10 to 1 in 5 such cases).
may.basis: NF1-fine stay-through at K 0.5 m, 0.6 m: median 35–56 ppm, above 87 in 10–22 % of periods; 0.7 m 2–4 %; 1.1 m never
may.mustCarry: 推估 / Estimate; low confidence; near-still held wind (light wind from that side in about 1 % of reds, held 15 minutes much rarer); exact position; very still air in the model; moving half a metre removes it

may.zh: 推估：靠近排氣管時，一氧化碳是一陣一陣的：半公尺處最高的一秒通常約5–30 ppm，風從機車吹來或幾乎無風時可達100–300 ppm。
may.en: Estimate: near a tailpipe, carbon monoxide comes in second-long bursts: the highest second at half a metre is usually about 5–30 ppm, and 100–300 ppm when the wind blows from the scooters or the air is nearly still.
may.basis: K 0.5 m highest 1 s P50 across cases; NF1-fine; grid check says pushchair-height peaks are probably about 3 times higher than pack runs show
may.mustCarry: 推估 / Estimate; one-second values; uncertain about 3 times; not comparable with 15-minute or 1-hour guidelines

may.zh: 推估：風從機車吹向你時，嬰兒車高度（約0.7公尺）的廢氣可能是大人鼻子高度的兩倍左右。
may.en: Estimate: when the wind blows from the scooters to you, exhaust at pushchair height (about 0.7 m) can be about twice that at an adult's nose.
may.basis: S1-from 0.7/1.5 m ratio 1.8; measured kerbside ratios 1.1–1.8; S5-12b 3.8 and NF1-fine many times
may.mustCarry: 推估 / Estimate; range about the same to twice (more right behind a tailpipe in still air); not in every wind

may.zh: 推估：你聞到的味道是真的。站在一群怠速機車的下風處，紅燈期間大部分的秒數，廢氣濃度都高於一般人聞得到的程度。
may.en: Estimate: the smell is real. Downwind of a group of idling scooters, the exhaust is above the level most people can smell for most seconds of the red.
may.basis: S1-from: 76–97 % of seconds at or above 1 odour unit (D/T 6,800), 36–76 % (D/T 800); S5-12b 80 %; canyon cases 11–29 %
may.mustCarry: 推估 / Estimate; downwind; odour thresholds from 1960s–70s car-exhaust studies; range 'about half to nearly all seconds'

may.zh: 一氧化碳沒有味道。你聞到的是未燒完的汽油和不完全燃燒的產物，鼻子在十億分之幾的濃度就聞得到，所以味道很重不代表一氧化碳超過標準。
may.en: Carbon monoxide has no smell. What you smell is unburnt fuel and partial-combustion products, which the nose detects at parts per billion, so a strong smell does not mean carbon monoxide is above the guideline.
may.basis: odour thresholds (Nagata 2003; API 1995); simulation: smell above threshold while 15-min CO stays 5–25 times below 87 ppm

may.zh: 推估：對在路口待上一小時的人（攤販、交通警察），若風一直從機車吹來，苯的一小時平均可能達到美國加州1小時參考值的1到4倍。
may.en: Estimate: for someone who stays at a junction for an hour (vendors, traffic police), with the wind from the scooters, benzene can reach about 1 to 4 times California's 1-hour reference level.
may.basis: S1-from stay-through 1-h benzene 16–31 ppb at 0.5 m, 9–17 ppb at 1 m; S5-12b 12–24 ppb; reference 8.5 ppb
may.mustCarry: 推估 / Estimate; range 1–4 times; the reference was derived on a 6-hour basis; benzene emission share uncertain 5–10 times; held wind; not for a pedestrian waiting one red

may.zh: 推估：只有封閉空間，例如地下停車場、地下道或少通風的有頂候車區、裡面有幾十台機車怠速，才可能讓一氧化碳的15分鐘平均達到世界衛生組織的指引值。
may.en: Estimate: only an enclosed space — an underground car park, an underpass or a poorly ventilated covered waiting area with dozens of idling scooters — could generally bring the 15-minute carbon monoxide average up to the WHO value.
may.basis: mass balance (bounds.py); Hong Kong car parks 15-min means 39 ppm average, up to 362 ppm
may.mustCarry: 推估 / Estimate; not simulated; no Taiwanese measurement

may.zh: 推估：風從機車吹向騎樓時，騎樓裡1–3公尺處的一氧化碳比路緣低（平均約1–4 ppm），但不是乾淨的空氣。
may.en: Estimate: with the wind from the scooters toward an arcade, air 1–3 m inside the arcade is lower than at the kerb edge (about 1–4 ppm on average) but not clean.
may.basis: S5-12b AR probes: 0.6–3.6 ppm P50 against 7.5 ppm at the kerb edge
may.mustCarry: 推估 / Estimate; one light-wind red; build-up over many cycles not simulated

mustNot: Kerb carbon monoxide is above the WHO guideline (in any form, for a pedestrian waiting at a red light).
The smell shows the carbon monoxide is dangerous, high, or above a standard.
Any 1-second, 10-second or 90-second value set beside the WHO 15-minute (87 ppm) or 1-hour (31 ppm) value without conversion, e.g. 'peaks of 200 ppm, twice the WHO limit'.
'Far below the guideline' applied to second-long bursts, to people who stay at the kerb, or to a pushchair directly behind a tailpipe in near-still air.
The simulation matches (or validates against) the Kaohsiung kerb measurement.
Street canyons lower kerb exposure; a bigger pack in calmer air gives less exposure.
Arcades trap exhaust; or arcades are safe/clean.
Exceeds the NIOSH limit, without 'workplace ceiling, for seconds, in rare conditions (at most about 0.1–0.4 % of reds)'.
Hundreds of odour units, or any precise odour-unit number, as fact.
Children breathe twice as much carbon monoxide (as a general statement).
Standing N metres further away cuts your exposure by X.
Any statement about health effects, safety, cancer risk from one red, or 'harmless'.
Any number from S5-12 or S4-S5-12 (withdrawn), or from the canyon cases as a typical kerb value.
Any number without 推估 / Estimate and its range.
